system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s labels of **[STANDARD]**, **FINAL** and “agreed” do not establish Buyer approval. I would keep the following points open. The recommendations assume the SPA text matches the Seller’s summary; the operative clauses and DD documents still need checking.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20%)**. | A materially higher, enforceable cap, supported where possible by escrow or other security. | **Reject 20%; seek at least 50% of price**, because the proposed cap may not cover a substantial SaaS revenue, IP or compliance loss. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 aggregate **deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping** basket, with related claims aggregated and carve-outs for specific indemnities. | **Counter with AUD 10,000 / AUD 100,000 tipping**, because the draft leaves the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid losses with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; Seller seeks to extend that limit to all Claims by default. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with separate longer periods for tax, title, IP and specific indemnities. | **Reject the all-Claims default**, because some liabilities may emerge well after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties with at least a **100%-of-price cap** and a substantially longer claim period. | **Ring-fence fundamental claims**, because Buyer is paying for valid ownership of all shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to Claims “of any nature”. | Express preservation of fraud, intentional concealment and dishonest misrepresentation claims and remedies, without contractual caps or time bars. | **Add an overriding fraud carve-out**, because the blanket wording could otherwise be argued to restrict those claims. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** with enough detail to identify their nature and likely implications; no general or deemed disclosure. | **Reject blanket disclosure**, because uploading or publicly filing a document should not by itself qualify every warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable from data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; if unavoidable, limit it to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, not advisers or constructive knowledge. | **Delete the qualifier**, because it would shift the burden of incomplete Seller disclosure onto Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied when written consent is delivered. Disclosure confirms no final consent or proof of conditions. | A Completion condition requiring effective written consent **and satisfaction or Buyer-approved waiver of clause 11.3 conditions**, with no material adverse amendment. | **Do not complete on a bare consent letter**, because Bluefen represents about **30% of FY26 revenue**. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion. | Agreed payoff figure, repayment from Completion funds and effective discharge/release mechanics at Completion, including registrations. | **Make payoff and release simultaneous with Completion**, because Buyer must receive a debt-free, unencumbered company. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow as a Seller matter. | Seller funding or a price adjustment for amounts triggered by the sale, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs; confirm conditions. | **Itemise and allocate them in funds flow**, because omission risks Buyer bearing a transaction-generated liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is shown open, without payment proof or assignment. | Payment evidence, confirmatory transfer of Project Materials and a specific indemnity covering ownership, use and remediation losses, not just the fee. | **Expand the indemnity and require transfer evidence**, because paying AUD 180,000 alone may not establish the Company’s IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification remain unresolved. | Completion-stage investigation and evidence, preservation/remediation and notification analysis, plus a ring-fenced indemnity for this incident. | **Treat it as an identified open risk, not a confirmed breach**, because the available facts neither establish nor exclude significant exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Review all three together for timing, obligation, termination and accounting treatment; prohibit unapproved renewals before Completion. | **Reserve a price/funds-flow adjustment if accrued or unavoidable**, because the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** cannot be dismissed without that analysis. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller’s broad limitations and disclosures would apply across all Claims unless excepted. | An express hierarchy separating general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud, with tailored limits for each. | **Rewrite the limitation schedule by claim category**, because a general catch-all could nullify negotiated special protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100%. | Verify issued capital, legal and beneficial ownership, encumbrances, transfer restrictions and Completion transfer documents against registers and supporting records. | **Do not rely on DD-012 alone**, because a share-register entry does not resolve every title or encumbrance question. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says both are settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity with a statutory-period-plus-buffer claim window; robust IP ownership warranties and tailored protection for identified defects. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open**, because their exposure and discovery periods differ from ordinary general warranties. |

**Priority before signing:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay rights, the incident investigation and the funds-flow treatment of bonuses should be documented as concrete Completion protections—not left to general warranties.
=== END ADVICE ===
